value: white variety raised in Bresse has appellation d'origine contrôlée status as poulet de Bresse
regarded as a premium meat product

history_summary.value: Chickens from the Bresse region of eastern France were recorded as early as 1591 and gained a reputation as a premium table bird, but the breed nearly disappeared around 1900 before fancy breeders rebuilt it from white stock under a 1904 standard. The Bresse name received legal protection in 1936 and full appellation d'origine contrôlée status in 1957.
